HTTP Caching Overview

Caches store responses so subsequent requests can avoid repeating work. Fresh responses may be reused without contacting the origin, while stale responses can be revalidated with conditional requests.

Cache-Control directives such as max-age, no-store, and must-revalidate communicate reuse policy. Shared caches must respect private responses and authorization-sensitive content.

Validators like ETag and Last-Modified allow efficient confirmation that a cached copy is still current. When validation fails, the origin returns a full representation for replacement in the cache.
